one_line_contribution: That retrieved-experience memory harms agents by making them stop gathering evidence early rather than by supplying bad advice, evidenced by a token-matched outcome-redaction contrast (M2 vs M3) and by a harness-enforced evidence floor (M1+Fh) that a GEPA-searched instruction (G1) allegedly cannot match.
closest_prior_work: Xiong et al., arXiv:2505.16067 (experience-following / misaligned experience replay), which the proposal correctly identifies and concedes owns the phenomenon; what it leaves open is the mediator, so novelty rests entirely on the three downstream pieces. Two bodies of work the proposal does not engage threaten those pieces harder than 2505.16067 does. (a) The sufficient-context / abstention line (Joren et al., 'Sufficient Context: A New Lens on RAG Systems', ICLR 2025, and its successors) already establishes that LLM agents answer confidently on insufficient context, already operationalizes the exact binary 'evidence sufficiency' instrumented here, and already shows that context-driven premature answering drives error - meaning predictions 2 and 8 are close to re-measurements in a memory wrapper. (b) The citation-grounded generation line (Self-RAG, ALCE-style attribution, verify-before-answer scaffolds) is the evidence floor: 'the agent must list retrieved spans that support the answer before it may emit one, and the harness rejects it otherwise' is an existing technique, not a new intervention, so M1+Fh's novelty is only its use as an interaction probe. arXiv:2604.27003 (abstract procedural memory transfers better than trajectories) is correctly flagged as a near-miss on M2>M3; the redaction design is a genuine tightening of it, and is the single most defensible novel element here.
strongest_objection: The headline causal test is underpowered by the proposal's own arithmetic. Measurement and Noise Control states the memory x floor interaction - a difference of two paired differences - is detectable at ~6 points at n=500. Prediction 3 predicts breaks under M1 of ~50/500 = 10 points, cut by >=50% = a 5-point reduction, against an M0+Fh gain of '<1/3 of that' = <1.7 points. The predicted interaction is therefore ~3.3 points, roughly half the stated MDE. The single experiment that the proposal designates as 'the causal test' (Analysis 2) is thus specified to produce an effect it cannot resolve, and every arm downstream of it - M6, M7, and the entire division-of-labour comparison in Analysis 4, which compares M1+Fs and G1 against a 5-point M1+Fh benefit and asks whether they recover less than a third of it, i.e. resolving ~1.7-point differences - inherits that problem. The proposal is otherwise unusually rigorous about power, which makes this internally inconsistent rather than merely optimistic. Compounding it: the headline quantity is written as (breaks under M1 - breaks under M1+Fh) - (errors under M0 - errors under M0+Fh), which mixes a paired relative measure ('breaks', defined against M0) with an absolute one ('errors'), and never says whether breaks under M1+Fh are scored against M0 or M0+Fh; those two choices give different numbers and one of them makes the interaction partly definitional. Second-order but serious: even a clean positive interaction is confounded with error composition. M1 has more search-remediable errors available to fix than M0 by construction (that is what 'break' means), so a larger absolute floor benefit under M1 is the base-rate expectation, not evidence for a memory-specific mechanism; the comparison needs stratification on matched baseline error type or a relative-risk formulation, not raw absolute points. Third, prediction 6 - the claim the abstract calls 'sharp and risky' - is close to tautological. That a harness-enforced constraint outperforms the same constraint stated as text is the standing result of the instruction-following literature; M1+Fs is near-certain to lose, and G1 is a 400-rollout search over the instruction slot whose failure Risk 5 pre-emptively downgrades to 'inconclusive on enforcement-vs-discovery' if no verification language emerges. The prediction is thus arranged so that the interesting outcome is near-guaranteed and the uninteresting one is unreportable, which is the opposite of risk.
what_would_fix_it: (1) Re-derive the power for Analysis 2 as the primary endpoint and size n to it: either raise the paired test set (n~1200-1500 rather than 500, which the 40-node-hour budget can absorb by cutting the M3, M4 and M5 arms to a smaller subset), or select the test split enriched for instances where the precheck bank actually retrieves outcome-bearing near-neighbours, so the M1 break rate is 20-25% rather than 10% and a halving is a 10-12 point swing. State the interaction MDE and the predicted interaction in the same units in the same paragraph. (2) Fix the estimand: define breaks under every floor arm against a single fixed reference (M0, no floor), report the interaction as a ratio of break rates with a stratified analysis conditioning on M0 error type, and show the floor benefit is not explained by M1's richer supply of search-remediable errors. (3) Make prediction (iii) risky by giving the instruction slot its fair chance and by testing the other half of the division of labour: run GEPA (or a ReasoningBank-style rewriter) on the memory/demonstration slot at the same reflective budget, and run G1+Fh. 'Instruction search cannot repair a demonstration-slot pathology' is only a division-of-labour claim if the demonstration-slot search is shown to repair it. (4) Disentangle the mediator from the intervention. The title claims agents stop looking; the intervention that works requires them to cite. Add an arm that raises search depth without any justification requirement and with the sufficiency check applied only silently post hoc (M6 is close but keeps no sufficiency requirement at all), and an arm where memory is injected only after the agent has completed its own retrieval - if late injection removes the harm, the mechanism is 'never starts looking', not 'stops looking early', and the paper's central noun changes. (5) Pre-register the leakage audit threshold for M2 and state what leakage rate voids the redaction contrast, since procedural text in multi-hop QA ('look up the 1994 record holder, then their birthplace') encodes the answer path almost completely and a high leak rate makes M2 an outcome arm in disguise.
missing_baseline: A searched demonstration-slot repair: GEPA (or any reflective optimizer) applied to memory content itself - rewriting, filtering or abstracting the frozen bank - at the same 400-rollout budget and the same reflective access to shortcutting failures. The track's question is instructions versus demonstrations; the plan searches only the instruction slot (G1/G0) and pits it against a hand-written control-flow guard, so 'the repair belongs to the control flow' is asserted without ever testing whether it belongs to the demonstration slot. M2 is a hand-written demonstration-slot repair and is predicted to work, which makes the omission of its searched counterpart conspicuous: if a memory-slot optimizer matches M1+Fh, the correct conclusion is 'this is a demonstration-slot problem fixable in the demonstration slot', not 'prompt optimization cannot own it'. Also absent and cheap: G1+Fh (are instruction search and the floor additive or redundant?); a late-injection arm (memory revealed only after the agent's own retrieval completes), which is the strongest content-free competitor to the floor and costs no extra calls; and an abstention/'insufficient evidence' baseline, since converting a memory-induced wrong answer into a refusal is a live alternative repair that the fix/break table would score very differently.
preprint_collision: Above average for this kind of section and clearly done in good faith: it names one genuine partial collision (2505.16067) and concedes the phenomenon rather than claiming it, flags 2604.27003 as a near-miss on the M2/M3 contrast, states an explicit gap, and admits it could not sweep ICLR/NeurIPS 2026 portals. It also volunteers that an earlier draft carried a dozen unverifiable forward-dated IDs, which is honest but should make a reviewer check the surviving IDs. The check is nonetheless incomplete in exactly the region where this proposal's own mechanism lives. It searched the memory literature and not the stopping/sufficiency literature: nothing on sufficient-context and abstention in RAG (Joren et al., ICLR 2025 and successors), which already instruments the identical 'do the supporting spans appear in this episode's retrievals' binary and already reports models answering confidently without them; nothing on citation-grounded/verify-before-answer generation (Self-RAG, attribution-constrained decoding), which is what the evidence floor is; and nothing substantive on premature stopping in search/deep-research agents beyond a one-line dismissal of 'AgentStop-style early-exit papers' as the mirror image. That dismissal is too quick - efficiency-motivated early-exit work measures the exact endpoints proposed here (tool calls before answer, accuracy lost to stopping early) and several such papers report the accuracy cost of truncated search, which is prediction 1 in the other direction. No search is reported for the specific conjunction 'retrieved experience' + 'stopping/termination', which is the claim. So: no named preprint that I can point to makes this exact claim, but the check does not establish that, and its blind spot is not peripheral - it is the mediator and the intervention.
